meta.titre: The Mammalian Heart: chambers, valves, blood flow and the myogenic beat
meta.sous_theme: Structure and working of the human heart

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Human Biology past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A footballer in Bamenda sprints for the ball, stops, and feels his heart pounding in his chest. That pump has not rested since before he was born. It keeps two separate streams of blood moving: one to the lungs and one to the rest of the body. At the GCE you are asked to name the parts of a heart diagram, to say what each valve does, and to explain why the heart can beat without being told to. Knowing the structure well lets you answer all of these in a few lines.

items: Blood is a liquid tissue that carries oxygen, food and waste around the body.
Arteries carry blood away from the heart and veins carry blood towards the heart.
Oxygenated blood is rich in oxygen; deoxygenated blood has given up much of its oxygen to the tissues.

sections.titre: Chambers, vessels, valves and the heart beat
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Parts of the heart
The heart is a muscular pump with four chambers: two thin-walled **atria** (upper chambers) and two thick-walled **ventricles** (lower chambers). A muscular wall called the **septum** divides the left side from the right side, so oxygenated and deoxygenated blood never mix.

| Part | Job |
|---|---|
| Right atrium | Receives deoxygenated blood from the body through the **venae cavae** |
| Right ventricle | Pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs through the **pulmonary artery** |
| Left atrium | Receives oxygenated blood from the lungs through the **pulmonary veins** |
| Left ventricle | Pumps oxygenated blood to the whole body through the **aorta**; it has the thickest wall |
| Tricuspid valve | Between right atrium and right ventricle |
| Bicuspid valve | Between left atrium and left ventricle |
| Semi-lunar valves | At the start of the aorta and of the pulmonary artery |
| Tendinous cords | Thin strings joining the atrio-ventricular valves to the papillary muscles in the ventricle wall |
| Coronary arteries | Branch from the aorta and supply the heart muscle itself with oxygen and glucose |

### Path of blood
Venae cavae, right atrium, tricuspid valve, right ventricle, semi-lunar valve, pulmonary artery, lungs, pulmonary veins, left atrium, bicuspid valve, left ventricle, semi-lunar valve, aorta, body. Blood therefore passes through the heart twice in one complete circuit (double circulation).

### Why the left ventricle is thicker
It must push blood at high pressure all around the body. The right ventricle only sends blood to the nearby lungs, so its wall is thinner. The atria only push blood a short distance into the ventricles, so their walls are the thinnest.

variantes.nom: Valves and the sounds of the heart
variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked what valves do or why blood flows in one direction only
variantes.contenu_markdown:
- The **atrio-ventricular valves** (tricuspid and bicuspid) open when the atria contract, and shut when the ventricles contract, so blood cannot flow back into the atria. The tendinous cords stop them from turning inside out.
- The **semi-lunar valves** have three pocket-shaped cusps. They shut when the ventricles relax, so blood in the artery cannot flow back into the ventricle.
- The two heart sounds, often written "lub-dub", are made by the valves closing: first the atrio-ventricular valves, then the semi-lunar valves.

variantes.nom: Myogenic heart and its blood supply
variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked what myogenic means or why a blocked coronary artery is dangerous
variantes.contenu_markdown:
A **myogenic** muscle starts its own contractions. Heart muscle contracts and relaxes rhythmically even without a nerve impulse, because a small patch of special tissue in the wall of the right atrium (the **pacemaker**) starts each beat. Nerves and the hormone adrenaline do not start the beat; they only make it faster or slower.

The heart muscle needs a constant supply of oxygen and glucose. If a coronary artery is blocked by a blood clot or fatty deposits, part of the muscle is starved and may die. This is a **heart attack**. A diet rich in fatty food, smoking and lack of exercise raise the risk.

sections.enonce_markdown: A red blood cell is in the vena cava of a student at rest. Describe the route it takes through the heart until it enters the aorta, naming every chamber and valve passed, and explain why the wall of the chamber that finally pushes it into the aorta is thicker than the others. *(6 marks)*

etapes.justification: "Describe the route" asks for an ordered list, and "explain why" asks for a reason linked to a function.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Two parts: the ordered path from vena cava to aorta, and the thickness of one wall.

etapes.justification: Blood from the body is deoxygenated and always enters the right atrium first.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Vena cava, right atrium, tricuspid valve, right ventricle.

etapes.action: Go to the lungs and back
etapes.justification: The right ventricle sends the blood out through a semi-lunar valve to the lungs, where it picks up oxygen.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Semi-lunar valve, pulmonary artery, lungs, pulmonary vein, left atrium.

etapes.justification: The left atrium sends the blood through the bicuspid valve into the left ventricle.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Bicuspid valve, left ventricle, semi-lunar valve, aorta.

etapes.justification: The wall thickness is linked to the distance and the pressure needed.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The left ventricle must push blood at high pressure to the whole body, so it has a thicker muscular wall than the right ventricle.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The cell passes from the vena cava into the right atrium, through the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle, then through a semi-lunar valve into the pulmonary artery. After the lungs it returns by the pulmonary vein to the left atrium, goes through the bicuspid valve into the left ventricle and leaves through a semi-lunar valve into the aorta. The left ventricle has the thickest wall because it pumps blood at high pressure to all parts of the body, while the right ventricle sends blood only to the nearby lungs.

items.erreur_markdown: The pulmonary artery carries oxygenated blood to the lungs, like every artery.
items.pourquoi_faux: The word "artery" means a vessel taking blood away from the heart, not a vessel carrying oxygenated blood. The pulmonary artery leaves the right ventricle with deoxygenated blood.
items.correction_markdown: The pulmonary artery carries **deoxygenated** blood to the lungs; the pulmonary veins carry **oxygenated** blood back to the left atrium.

items.erreur_markdown: The tricuspid valve is on the left and the bicuspid valve on the right.
items.pourquoi_faux: The sides are reversed. The bicuspid valve has two flaps and guards the opening into the left ventricle.
items.correction_markdown: Tricuspid valve: right side. Bicuspid valve: left side.

items.erreur_markdown: Myogenic means that the brain sends impulses to make the heart beat.
items.pourquoi_faux: That is the meaning of neurogenic. A myogenic heart beats by itself; the nerves only change the rate.
items.correction_markdown: Myogenic: the heart muscle starts its own contractions, without a nerve impulse.

items.erreur_markdown: On a diagram the left ventricle is drawn on the left of the page.
items.pourquoi_faux: A heart diagram is usually drawn as the doctor sees it, facing the patient, so the left side of the heart is on the right of the page.
items.correction_markdown: The thick-walled chamber on the right of the page is the **left ventricle**.

items.enonce_markdown: Name (a) the vessel that brings blood from the lungs to the heart, (b) the chamber that receives this blood, (c) the vessel that carries blood from the heart to the whole body, (d) the structure that separates the left and right ventricles.
A child is born with a bicuspid valve that does not close tightly. (a) In which direction does blood leak when the ventricles contract? (b) Explain why the child may tire quickly during games.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Blood leaks backwards from the **left ventricle into the left atrium**, because the valve that should shut the opening does not seal it.

(b) Each beat sends less blood into the aorta, so less oxygen and glucose reach the muscles, and less respiration can release energy. The child therefore tires quickly.

items.enonce_markdown: The volume of blood pumped by the left ventricle in one minute is called the cardiac output: cardiac output = heart rate $\times$ stroke volume (the volume pumped at each beat). At rest a student has a heart rate of 72 beats per minute and a stroke volume of 70 cm$^3$. During a race the heart rate is 132 beats per minute and the stroke volume is 85 cm$^3$. (a) Calculate the cardiac output at rest. (b) Calculate it during the race. (c) By how many times has it increased (1 decimal place)? (d) Explain why the body needs this change.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) $72 \times 70 = 5040$ cm$^3$ per minute, which is **5.04 dm$^3$ per minute**.

(b) $132 \times 85 = 11\,220$ cm$^3$ per minute, which is **11.22 dm$^3$ per minute**.

(c) $11\,220 \div 5040 = 2.226...$, so the output has increased about **2.2 times**.

(d) Working muscles respire faster, so they need more oxygen and glucose and must lose more carbon dioxide. A larger cardiac output delivers more blood to them and removes the waste more quickly.

items_markdown: The heart has four chambers: two atria that receive blood and two ventricles that pump it out. The septum keeps the two sides apart.
Blood path: vena cava, right atrium, right ventricle, pulmonary artery, lungs, pulmonary vein, left atrium, left ventricle, aorta.
Tricuspid valve on the right, bicuspid valve on the left; semi-lunar valves at the base of the aorta and pulmonary artery. All valves prevent backflow.
The left ventricle has the thickest wall because it pumps blood at high pressure to the whole body.
The heart is myogenic: it starts its own beat, and nerves and adrenaline only change the rate. Coronary arteries feed the heart muscle, and a blockage causes a heart attack.
